design_summary: I propose a two-layer common foundation that keeps the reviewed S02 semantics but repairs the type sketch where it is either unexpressive, circular, or not implementable as written. Layer 1 is a neutral observation carrier (observations.qnt) that is lossless against the frozen Python Core result: total account map with zero meaning absent (Core forbids stored zeros, so this is injective), NoInt versus IntValue(0) for choices, ordered warnings with requested/paid, ordered payments, generic continuation, minimum time, reductions, exact error string. Two corrections to the sketch: the Core projection and settlement evidence become explicitly optional (NoCoreProjection for B/C/D and for authority-only actions such as cancellation, so no fabricated Core result is ever needed), and the observation carries the neutral supplied input (deposit-like, choice-like, or none) plus a rejection reason type separate from Core errors. Layer 2 is an authorization library (authorization.qnt) that supplies only arithmetic and predicates. Policies are branch-structured: a signed policy is a finite list of branches, each with a trigger over observable facts (transaction time, supplied decision, predecessor consumption state), required incoming effects, and allowed effects; a principal allows a proposal iff some branch triggers and policyAllows(branch.required, branch.allowed, actual) holds. The flat requiredEffects+conditions shape in the sketch cannot express the swap disposition and must not be adopted. Authority conjunction ranges over the owners of every debited source location; recipients are not signers. Fill, cancellation, and recovery all flow through one verify-then-commit pipeline: a verification record binds the observation, predecessor context, environment, consumption revision, and evidence dispositions; commit requires an exact match of the applicable bindings. The prepared cancellation of the sketch is simply a verified cancellation observation with empty effects bound to a consumption revision, so both race outcomes arise symmetrically from two in-flight verifications at the same revision. The harness keeps a per-proposal-kind lifecycle map (FillSlot1, FillSlot2, CancelParent, RecoverEscrow) rather than one scalar phase and one verification slot, so slot-2 completion, post-cancel slot-2 rejection, stale-fill rejection, and stale-cancel rejection are all reachable and observable. Recovery is a normal proposal under Alice nonce 1 whose quantity is the actual escrow balance from the ledger, never the parent's remaining allowance; it goes through resolve/check/sign in the lifecycle. Time is finite and monotone: physicalTime ranges over {1,2,100,101}, proposals carry an adversarial transactionTime from the same set that must not exceed physicalTime at verification, which closes future-dating while keeping time_before_state observable. Environment freshness is defined per evidence class: state and verification evidence bind the full environment; signature evidence binds mechanism and version only, so SignBeforeResolve remains reachable. Terminal states are defined by an explicit predicate and are the only states with a stutter; Apalache deadlock detection stays on. I recommend reviewing the carrier separately because three candidates and the independent E00 checker consume it, and its losslessness should be pinned by its own hash and a small emission-rule test before authorization logic bakes in expectations.

required_changes.location: Policy, evidence, and authority shapes: Policy[plan] with requiredEffects, allowedEffects, conditions
required_changes.defect: A flat policy with one requiredEffects list and a conjunction of conditions cannot express conditional consideration. The swap disposition (nonce 1 per principal, only two nonces per principal) must permit settlement requiring the counter-leg, voluntary refund requiring nothing, and deadline refund requiring nothing. With effects.policyAllows(required, allowed, actual) the only two encodings are both wrong.
required_changes.counterexample: Fixture: canonical swap after both deposits, time 2, Alice disposition policy nonce 1. Encoding X: requiredEffects=[Escrow(Bob,B)->Wallet(Alice) 20]. Then a voluntary refund proposal actual=[Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Alice) 10, Escrow(Bob,B)->Wallet(Bob) 20] fails submultiset(required, actual), so voluntary-refund and deadline-refund witnesses are unreachable under Alice's only disposition nonce. Encoding Y: requiredEffects=[] and allowedEffects=[Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Bob) 10, Escrow(Bob,B)->Wallet(Alice) 20, refunds...]. Then actual=[Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Bob) 10] alone satisfies submultiset(required, actual) and submultiset(actual, allowed); affected principals={Alice}; Bob is not consulted; Alice pays 10 and receives nothing. This is exactly control 2 (executed-artifact-substitution) passing the common check.
required_changes.proposed_change: Replace requiredEffects/allowedEffects/conditions with branches: List[PolicyBranch], PolicyBranch = {trigger: List[Trigger], requiredEffects: List[Transfer], allowedEffects: List[Transfer]}. principalAllows(policy, observation, context) = branches.exists(b => triggersHold(b.trigger, observation, context) and policyAllows(b.requiredEffects, b.allowedEffects, observation.effects)). Keep debitLocations at policy level. Swap disposition branches: settle {trigger [DecisionIs('settle',1)], required [counter-leg], allowed [both legs]}, voluntary {trigger [DecisionIs('settle',0)], required [], allowed [both refunds]}, deadline {trigger [TimeAtOrAfter(100), NoDecision], required [], allowed [both refunds]}.
required_changes.acceptance_test: authorization_test.qnt: (1) one-legged settlement actual=[Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Bob) 10] with decision settle=1 is rejected by allAffectedPrincipalsAllow; (2) full settlement is accepted; (3) voluntary refund with decision settle=0 is accepted; (4) deadline refund at transactionTime 100 with no decision is accepted; all four under the same nonce-1 policies for Alice and Bob.

required_changes.defect: conditionsHold receives the candidate-declared outcome label and can satisfy a condition from it. The label is a solver/candidate-supplied boolean, which the design forbids as authorization evidence. The observation also lacks the supplied input, so the common checker cannot independently establish that a refund branch was actually triggered by Bob's choice.
required_changes.counterexample: Swap after both deposits, time 2, Bob has not chosen. Mallory proposes observation{effects=[Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Alice) 10, Escrow(Bob,B)->Wallet(Bob) 20], outcome=VoluntaryRefund, transactionTime=2}. Alice's and Bob's disposition policies each have condition RequiresOutcome(VoluntaryRefund) for the refund branch. conditionsHold reads observation.outcome and returns true; policyAllows passes; the swap is unwound before any decision. Candidate D has no interpreter to catch this; the common check is the only guard and it accepted a label.
required_changes.proposed_change: Add input: NeutralInput to CandidateObservation, NeutralInput = NoInput | DepositLike({location: Location, asset: Asset, quantity: int}) | ChoiceLike({id: str, chooser: Principal, chosen: int}). Define triggers only over observable facts: DecisionIs(id, value), NoDecision, TimeBefore(t), TimeAtOrAfter(t), ParentCancelled(key), PredecessorSlotUsed(key, slot). Make outcome a derived classification classifyOutcome(observation, predecessorContext) and add invariant declaredOutcomeMatches: observation.outcome == classifyOutcome(...); the candidate label is display data, not an authorization input.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Test: the mislabeled refund above is rejected because NoDecision does not match the voluntary branch and TimeAtOrAfter(100) fails at time 2. Mutant: replace classifyOutcome with the declared label; the test must then wrongly accept, proving the check depends on the input field.

required_changes.defect: The Core projection and the settlement coreResult are mandatory fields, but B, C, and D have no Core projection in the lifecycle-extension slice, and even A's cancellation is an authority-only action with no Core transaction. Every such observation would have to invent a CoreResultObservation, which is fake settlement evidence and makes the settlement-evidence-level property untestable. Rejected(CoreError) also conflates non-Core rejections (stale evidence, unauthorized debit) with frozen Core error codes.
required_changes.counterexample: Candidate D, installment slot-1 fill: observation requires coreProjection: CoreResultObservation[c]. Builder supplies accepted=true, payments=[5 to Bob], reductions=1. SettlementEvidence{coreResult=that value, level=CoreResultEvidence, disposition=EvidenceValid}. verificationValid has no way to distinguish this from A's real projection, so the property 'a settlement claim does not exceed its declared evidence level' is vacuously satisfiable by any candidate. Second: a stale-environment rejection in D has no CoreError value; Rejected(CoreErrorCode('stale')) is not a frozen Core code and validFrozenCoreError must reject it, so the observation type cannot represent the rejection at all.
required_changes.proposed_change: type CoreProjection[c] = NoCoreProjection | CoreProjected(CoreResultObservation[c]). Use it in CandidateObservation and in SettlementEvidence (coreResult: CoreProjection[c]). Invariant: level == CoreResultEvidence implies coreResult is CoreProjected and disposition consistent; NoCoreProjection forces level == AbstractModelEvidence. type RejectionReason = CoreRejected(CoreError) | UnauthorizedEffect | StaleBindings | EvidenceMissing | ConsumptionConflict; SemanticOutcome uses Rejected(RejectionReason). validCoreObservation stays restricted to CoreProjected values.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Tests: (1) an observation with NoCoreProjection and level CoreResultEvidence fails verificationValid; (2) A's deadline pair (no input at 100 commits refunds; input at 100 yields CoreRejected(CoreErrorCode('contract_closed')) with the complete predecessor state) round-trips through CoreProjected; (3) a D observation with NoCoreProjection and AbstractModelEvidence is accepted.

required_changes.location: Pure-function interface: recoveryTransfer, canRecover, applyRecoveryLedger, applyRecoveryAuthority; harness actions verifyRecovery, commitRecovery
required_changes.defect: Recovery has a parallel code path that bypasses computeVerification and canCommit, so it is not subject to environment freshness, state evidence, version binding, or transaction-time checks. recoveryTransfer(parent, entry) takes no ledger, so its quantity can only come from entry.remainingAllowance, which is authority, not money. The design requires financial value and remaining authorization to be tracked separately.
required_changes.counterexample: Path A (stale environment): cancel-wins path, recovery policy nonce 1 binds ImplementationV1; changeEnvironment sets implementationVersion=V2; canRecover(recoveryPolicy, parent, entry, registry, ledger, actual) has no environment argument, so commitRecovery is enabled and refunds under a version the policy did not bind, violating authority-bindings. Path B (money/authority conflation): fixture variant with escrow balance 8 and budget 10 (a residual-expansion style mutant of the initial ledger): after slot 1, entry.remainingAllowance=5 but balance(Escrow(Alice,A))=3; recoveryTransfer yields quantity 5; canApply fails so recovery is unreachable, or if canApply is not consulted the ledger goes to -2. Either way the common model computed a refund from authority instead of balance.
required_changes.proposed_change: Delete the four recovery-specific functions. Recovery is a CandidateObservation with outcome Recovery, effects=[Transfer(parent.source, Wallet(parent.key.principal), parent.asset, balance(ledger, parent.source, parent.asset))], input NoInput. Its policy (Alice nonce 1) has one branch with trigger [ParentCancelled(parentKey)], required [], allowed [that exact transfer under SignAfterResolve; under SignBeforeResolve allowed is bounded by maximumQuantity=10 with a residual predicate quantity == current escrow balance evaluated at verification]. It flows through computeVerification/canCommit like every other proposal. Add pure def recoveryQuantity(ledger: Ledger, parent: Parent[p]): int = balance(ledger, parent.source, parent.asset).
required_changes.acceptance_test: Both profiles: cancel-wins refunds 10, fill-wins refunds 5, each via executionVerify+commit with the recovery kind. Negative: after sign of the recovery policy bound to V1, changeEnvironment to V2 makes commit of the recovery rejected (StaleBindings); recovery with quantity 10 after a first fill is rejected by canApply and by the residual predicate.

required_changes.location: Environment.physicalTime: int; TRANSACTION_TIMES; computeVerification/verificationValid time rules
required_changes.defect: No relation is specified between the proposal's transactionTime and environment.physicalTime, so a solver can future-date a proposal to satisfy AtOrAfterDeadline and Core's timeout reduction at physical time 1. Separately, physicalTime: int is unbounded, so the state space is infinite and Apalache can only claim bounded-depth exploration.
required_changes.counterexample: Swap after Alice's deposit only, physicalTime=1. Mallory proposes observation{transactionTime=101, input=NoInput, effects=[Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Alice) 10]} with A's coreProjection computed by compute_transaction(deposit_b_when, state{alice:10,min_time:1}, None, now=101): timeout to Close, refund payment, accepted. Alice's deadline branch trigger TimeAtOrAfter(100) is evaluated on transactionTime=101 and holds. verificationValid only requires transactionTime in TRANSACTION_TIMES. The refund commits at physical time 1, preempting Bob's deposit and the settlement, without any policy permitting an early refund.
required_changes.proposed_change: Bound physicalTime to TRANSACTION_TIMES = Set(1,2,100,101) with changeEnvironment advancing to a strictly greater member. verificationValid and canCommit require observation.transactionTime <= record.currentEnvironment.physicalTime and transactionTime in TRANSACTION_TIMES. Past-dated proposals remain allowed so Core's time_before_state is observable through the projection; future-dated proposals are rejected with StaleBindings before Core semantics are consulted.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Tests: (1) transactionTime=101 at physicalTime=1 is rejected; (2) a commit at time 2 followed by a proposal at time 1 with physicalTime=2 produces CoreRejected(CoreErrorCode('time_before_state')) with the complete predecessor state; (3) verify --backend apalache reports finite-state exploration with the time domain enumerated.

required_changes.defect: environmentFresh is one predicate over the whole Environment record. If it is equality, signature evidence bound at signing time goes stale on any physicalTime or anchor advance, which the SignBeforeResolve profile requires by construction (signing precedes resolution and the state changes that resolution depends on).
required_changes.counterexample: SignBeforeResolve swap: Alice checks the bounded intent and signs at environment E1={physicalTime 1, Anchor0, V1, LocalCheckerV1}; Bob's deposit commits and advances the anchor to Anchor1 and physical time to 2; the settlement plan is resolved and verified at E2. computeVerification requires environmentFresh(signatureEvidence(Alice).boundEnvironment, E2) which is false under equality, disposition=EvidenceInvalid. The before-resolve-execution witness is unreachable in every path, since some environment change must occur between signing and resolution for that profile to mean anything.
required_changes.proposed_change: Define per-class freshness: signatureFresh(bound, current) = bound.enforcementMechanism == current.enforcementMechanism and bound.implementationVersion == current.implementationVersion (time handled by Validity); stateFresh = full equality including stateAnchor and physicalTime for state evidence and for the predecessorContext bound in a verification record; effectFresh = full equality. Document that a policy validity window and the transactionTime bound (RC-05) govern time.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Both profiles reach settlement, voluntary refund, and deadline refund. Negative: verification with state evidence bound to Anchor0 after the anchor advanced to Anchor1 is rejected; signature evidence bound to LocalCheckerV1 after the mechanism advances to V2 is rejected.

required_changes.defect: One scalar LifecyclePhase and one verification slot cannot represent a fill in flight concurrently with a prepared cancellation or a recovery, cannot distinguish Committed-after-slot-1 from a terminal state, and the action list has no slot-2 pipeline and no stale-fill rejection. requirements.json lists second-installment-completion as a witness, and the design requires 'the losing operation cannot consume the same authority again' to be observable for both race orders.
required_changes.counterexample: Sketch harness, cancel-wins order: executionVerify(fill slot 1) at consumption revision 0 sets verification=SomeVerification(r0); prepareCancel; commitFreshCancel advances the entry to revision 1. Now commitFirstFill is guarded false by canCommit (consumption state mismatch), but no action records that rejection, and the only enabled actions are verifyRecovery/commitRecovery. The fill's loss is never observed, so the cancel-wins witness has no 'rejected stale fill' step. Second: after commitFirstFill the phase is Committed with verification cleared; there is no action that resolves or verifies slot 2, so second-installment-completion (paid 10, escrow 0) is unreachable.
required_changes.proposed_change: type ProposalKind = FillSlot1 | FillSlot2 | CancelParent | RecoverEscrow. HarnessState has phase: ProposalKind -> ProposalPhase, verification: ProposalKind -> OptionalVerification, preSign: ProposalKind -> OptionalPreSignCheck. Actions are parameterized by kind: resolve(k), preSignCheck(k), sign(k), executionVerify(k), commit(k), rejectStale(k). CancelParent is an observation with empty effects verified against the current consumption revision; prepareCancel is executionVerify(CancelParent). commit(k) requires canCommit against the current context; rejectStale(k) is enabled exactly when a verification exists and canCommit is false, and it records RejectedPhase for k. Terminal predicate per RC-09.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Runs: (1) fill-wins: verify(Cancel@rev0), verify(Fill1@rev0), commit(Fill1), rejectStale(Cancel), verify(Cancel@rev1), commit(Cancel), verify(Recover)=5, commit(Recover); (2) cancel-wins: verify(Fill1@rev0), verify(Cancel@rev0), commit(Cancel), rejectStale(Fill1), recover 10; (3) completion: Fill1, Fill2, escrow 0, paid 10, Cancel disabled (remainingAllowance 0), Recover disabled (balance 0), state terminal; (4) after (1), verify(Fill2) is rejected with ConsumptionConflict. All under both profiles.

required_changes.location: Harness state and action boundary: 'The recovery policy uses Alice nonce 1'; actions verifyRecovery, commitRecovery only
required_changes.defect: The recovery policy is pre-registered in the fixture and never resolved, pre-sign checked, or signed in the lifecycle. The observation design requires disposition-type policies to be explicitly signed in the model, and requires recovery to be independently authorized under both profiles. In addition, under SignAfterResolve the recovery plan quantity depends on which race outcome occurs, and with a single recovery nonce a registered plan for 10 cannot be replaced after fill-wins unless a supersession rule exists.
required_changes.counterexample: SignAfterResolve: resolve(Recover) with plan refund 10 while the parent is at revision 0, preSignCheck, sign registers Alice nonce 1 as AuthorityRegistered(refund 10). Then Fill1 commits (escrow 5). canCommit for the recovery is false forever (canApply fails, plan quantity 10 != balance 5). canRegisterAuthority requires AuthorityVacant, so no fresh recovery policy can be registered under nonce 1, and there are only two nonces. Escrow 5 is stranded with no enabled action except environment changes: an unintended deadlock that a guarded terminal predicate would have to mislabel as terminal.
required_changes.proposed_change: Recovery uses the full per-kind pipeline (RC-07). Registration rule: canRegisterAuthority(registry, sp) holds if the key is AuthorityVacant, or AuthorityRegistered(old) with old.signatureToken.policyRevision < sp.signatureToken.policyRevision; a Consumed key is never re-registrable. Bound policyRevision to {0,1}. Any pre-sign check or verification record bound to a superseded revision is stale and rejected. Add negative control stale-recovery-plan: the superseded refund-10 verification must be rejected after the refund-5 policy is registered.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Both profiles reach recovery after both race outcomes with the recovery policy signed in the trace (signature action observable). Negative: re-registration of a Consumed key is rejected; a verification bound to policyRevision 0 is rejected after revision 1 registers; nonce 0 is never reused for recovery.

required_changes.location: LifecyclePhase; 'There is no blanket stutter'; requirements.json property nonterminal-enabled
required_changes.defect: The sketch has no terminal predicate and no stated deadlock discipline. Quint cannot express 'some action is enabled' as a state invariant, so nonterminal-enabled has no implementation as written. Without a guarded terminal stutter, Apalache reports every genuine terminal state as a deadlock; with a blanket stutter it hides real deadlocks (the design forbids this).
required_changes.counterexample: After Fill1, Fill2 (escrow 0, paid 10, allowance 0) no action is enabled. quint verify --backend apalache with default deadlock checking reports a deadlock on that state, indistinguishable from the stranded-escrow deadlock in RC-08. If the implementer adds action stutter = all { true, unchanged all } to silence it, the RC-08 deadlock is hidden and nonterminal-enabled is vacuous.
required_changes.proposed_change: Define pure def isTerminal(s) explicitly: every proposal kind is Committed or Rejected with no pending verification, and (escrow balance == 0 or the parent is cancelled and the recovery key is Consumed) or a candidate-declared terminal candidate state. Add exactly one guarded action terminalStutter = all { isTerminal(s), unchanged all }. Keep Apalache deadlock detection enabled; nonterminal-enabled is then discharged by the absence of reported deadlocks together with the invariant terminalConservation: isTerminal(s) implies escrow + Wallet(Bob,A) + Wallet(Alice,A) == 10 and no AuthorityRegistered key remains applicable.
required_changes.acceptance_test: verify passes with deadlock detection on; a mutant that deletes the recovery pipeline must produce an Apalache deadlock report on the cancelled-with-escrow state; a mutant that replaces the terminalStutter guard with true must fail a test asserting that stutter is disabled in a non-terminal state.

required_changes.location: Two-installment fixture: 'Existing When/Choice boundaries separate the payments in A's fixture'; 'A's recovery path uses a refund branch and Close'
required_changes.defect: The design only requires a boundary between the two payments. In frozen Core a Pay at the contract root reduces on any transaction, including a no-input one, so cancel-before-any-fill would pay Bob. The cancellation action must also be authority-only (no Core transaction), otherwise an Alice cancel choice that continues to Close performs cancellation and recovery in one Core transaction under one nonce, contradicting the two-nonce, two-transaction recovery design.
required_changes.counterexample: Fixture with root Pay(Escrow(Alice,A), Bob, 5, When(...)) and state {alice A:10}. compute_transaction(root, state, None, now=1): reduce_to_quiescence executes Pay (paid 5, payment to Bob, reductions 1) and stops at the When; supplied is None and the contract is When so the result is error input_required. Because input_required restores the original state the payment does not persist here, but any accepted transaction at all (for example the deposit-less first Choice input) carries the 5-unit payment in before.payments. There is no Core transaction in which Alice cancels while escrow remains 10 and Bob receives nothing, so cancel-wins/recovery-before-any-fill has no A projection. Second: if the Alice 'refund' Choice case continues directly to Close, that single transaction both revokes and refunds; the common harness cannot project commit(CancelParent) (empty effects) and commit(RecoverEscrow) (refund) onto it.
required_changes.proposed_change: Commit A's installment fixture shape in the common package as an abstraction-map requirement: root When(cases=[Choice('claim1',Bob,1,1) -> Pay 5 -> When(cases=[Choice('claim2',Bob,1,1) -> Pay 5 -> Close, Choice('refund',Alice,1,1) -> Close], timeout, Close), Choice('refund',Alice,1,1) -> Close], timeout, Close). Cancellation is an authority-only observation with NoCoreProjection and empty effects. Recovery projects onto Alice's refund Choice transaction. Agreement-legal claim2 after cancellation must fail the envelope; agreement-legal refund without cancellation must fail the recovery branch trigger ParentCancelled.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Hand-authored Core expectations in observations_test.qnt for: no-input at time 1 at the root (CoreRejected input_required, state preserved); claim1 at time 1 (accepted, payments=[5 to Bob], accounts alice A:5, reductions 1); refund at time 2 after cancellation (accepted, payments=[5 to Alice], accounts empty); and the deadline pair at time 100.

required_changes.location: BoundedIntent duplicates Policy fields; SignatureToken.principal/key; Policy.principal vs key.principal
required_changes.defect: The same authorization content exists in two places (Policy and PlanBinding.CompleteBoundedIntent) with no consistency predicate, so the two copies can disagree and it is undefined which one principalAllows consults.
required_changes.counterexample: Policy{principal Alice, key (Installment,Alice,0), branches allow 5 to Bob, binding CompleteBoundedIntent({allowedEffects [Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Mallory) 10], ...})}. If principalAllows reads the binding for SignBeforeResolve, Mallory receives 10 under a signature whose visible policy says 5 to Bob. If it reads the policy, the bounded intent that was pre-sign checked is not the content enforced.
required_changes.proposed_change: Remove duplicated fields from BoundedIntent; keep only assumptionManifest and the pinned enforcement identity. Add pure def validPolicy(p) = p.principal == p.key.principal and profile/binding variant agree (SignAfterResolve iff CompleteResolvedPlan) and validEffects over every branch; pure def validSignedPolicy(sp) = validPolicy(sp.policy) and sp.signatureToken.key == sp.policy.key and sp.signatureToken.principal == sp.policy.principal. Registration and verification require both.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Tests that each inconsistent combination (token key mismatch, profile/binding mismatch, principal/key mismatch) is rejected by canRegisterAuthority and by computeVerification.

required_changes.location: Pure-function interface signatures with bracketed type binders; HarnessState[state, continuation, artifact, plan] as harness state; effects.qnt initialLedger
required_changes.defect: Three implementability gaps. (a) The signatures use explicit type-parameter binders on operators (pure def f[c](...)); the supplied foundations use implicit lowercase type variables (consumption.qnt initialEntry(parent: Parent[p]): Entry[p]) and the sketch's form is not established by anything supplied. (b) A Quint state variable cannot have a polymorphic type, so a harness 'parameterized only by the four payload types' cannot declare var state: HarnessState[s,c,a,p]. (c) effects.initialLedger(aliceA, bobB) cannot express the pre-funded installment escrow.
required_changes.counterexample: authorization_harness.qnt with var harness: HarnessState[state, continuation, artifact, plan] fails typecheck because free type variables are not permitted in a var declaration; the installment init requires a Ledger with (Escrow({owner: Alice, asset: TokenA}), TokenA) -> 10 and (Wallet(Alice), TokenA) -> 0, which no supplied constructor produces.
required_changes.proposed_change: Write polymorphic pure defs with implicit lowercase type variables. Give the non-candidate harness concrete neutral payload types (type HarnessCandidateState = InstallmentPhase(int) | ...; type HarnessContinuation = NeutralContinuation; type HarnessArtifact = NeutralArtifact; type HarnessPlan = NeutralPlan(ProposalKind, int)) and instantiate the polymorphic library at those types; later candidate harnesses copy the action structure with their own concrete types. Add pure def ledgerWith(entries: Set[((Location, Asset), int)]): Ledger to effects.qnt (total over LEDGER_KEYS, zero elsewhere) and installmentInitialLedger = ledgerWith(Set(((Escrow({owner: Alice, asset: TokenA}), TokenA), 10))). Use const PROFILE: SigningProfile with two instantiations.
required_changes.acceptance_test: quint typecheck passes for effects.qnt, observations.qnt, authorization.qnt, authorization_harness.qnt instantiated twice (PROFILE = SignAfterResolve, SignBeforeResolve); validLedger(installmentInitialLedger) holds and totalAsset(installmentInitialLedger, TokenA) == 10.

required_changes.location: canSignAfterResolve(check, plan, current) requiring unchanged checkedContext
required_changes.defect: If the whole Context (including the authority registry of counterparties) must be unchanged between pre-sign check and signing, one principal's signature invalidates the other principal's already-completed pre-sign check. This is not a cycle, but it forbids the natural 'resolve, both check, both sign' path the design describes and forces a serialized re-check that the harness must then model.
required_changes.counterexample: Swap settlement, SignAfterResolve: preSignCheck(Alice) at context C0; preSignCheck(Bob) at C0; sign(Alice) registers Alice nonce 1 giving C1; canSignAfterResolve(checkBob, plan, C1) compares checkedContext C0 to C1 and fails. Bob must re-check. With the RC-07 per-kind phase map this shows up as Bob's phase regressing from PreSignChecked to Resolved, or as an unreachable sign(Bob) if no re-check action exists.
required_changes.proposed_change: Define applicableBindings(context, key) = {candidateState, ledger, environment restricted per RC-06, authorityRegistry.get(key), parentRegistry.get(key)} and compare only that in canSignAfterResolve and canSignBeforeResolve. Pre-sign checks are per principal and do not require counterparties' registrations; execution verification requires all affected principals' registrations. Document this as the resolution of the cyclic-prerequisite question: check depends on unsigned policy plus plan; sign depends on check; verify depends on all signatures; no predicate depends on its own output.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Test that from a resolved settlement with no disposition signatures, preSignCheck(Alice) then preSignCheck(Bob) then sign(Alice) then sign(Bob) succeeds, and the reverse principal order succeeds; and that signing with a substituted plan after the check is rejected (post-sign-plan-substitution).

required_changes.defect: affectedPrincipals is undefined. If it includes recipients, every installment fill and every swap payout requires a policy record for the receiving principal that the fixtures do not provide, and the conjunction fails on AuthorityVacant. If it includes only source owners, recipients are correctly not signers, matching 'every wallet or escrow debit needs applicable authority'.
required_changes.counterexample: Installment slot-1 fill: effects=[Escrow(Alice,A)->Wallet(Bob) 5]. Under the recipient-inclusive reading affectedPrincipals={Alice,Bob}; policies.get(Bob)=AuthorityVacant; allAffectedPrincipalsAllow=false for every fill; first-installment-residual is unreachable and the candidate fails the nonvacuity floor.
required_changes.proposed_change: pure def affectedPrincipals(effects) = effects.foldl(Set(), (s, e) => s.union(Set(ownerOf(e.source)))) with ownerOf(Wallet(p)) = p and ownerOf(Escrow(a)) = a.owner. allAffectedPrincipalsAllow requires for every affected principal q a non-vacant record whose policy has e.source in debitLocations for every actual effect e with ownerOf(e.source) == q, and principalAllows(q's policy, observation, context). Mallory can only be affected if a Mallory-owned location is debited, which the fixtures never fund.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Tests: the slot-1 fill is accepted with only Alice registered; an effect Wallet(Bob)->Wallet(Mallory) 1 with no Bob policy is rejected; Bob's choice input with effects debiting Alice's escrow requires Alice's policy branch, not Bob's.

required_changes.defect: The first fill moves Alice nonce 0 to AuthorityConsumed and claims the parent, but the second slot must be authorized by the same nonce through the ActiveParent entry. As sketched, canConsumeAuthority is the only applicability rule and it can only succeed on AuthorityRegistered, so slot 2 has no applicable authority. There is also no invariant tying AuthorityConsumed to the parent entry's Claimed state, so the two registries can drift under a mutant.
required_changes.counterexample: After commit(FillSlot1): authorityRegistry.get((Installment,Alice,0)) = AuthorityConsumed({policy, consumptionRevision 1}); parentRegistry entry = {claim Claimed(parent), usedSlots {1}, paid 5, remainingAllowance 5, cancelled false, revision 1}. executionVerify(FillSlot2) builds policies = Alice -> AuthorityConsumed(...); canConsumeAuthority requires Registered; verification disposition EvidenceInvalid; second-installment-completion unreachable. Drift mutant: applyConsumeSlot applied without applyConsumeAuthority leaves nonce 0 Registered while the entry is Claimed; a fresh standalone policy cannot register (key not vacant) but a replay of the original fill passes canConsumeAuthority again.
required_changes.proposed_change: Define applicableAuthority(registry, parentRegistry, key, kind): Registered for a first use (Fill1, Cancel from unclaimed, Recover, swap fund/dispose); Consumed with ActiveParent entry satisfying consumption.canConsumeSlot(parent, entry, 2, entry) for FillSlot2 and consumption.canCancelParent for a later cancellation. Add invariant registriesCoupled: for the installment key, registry record is AuthorityConsumed iff entry.claim is Claimed, and consumptionRevision == entry.revision. commit(FillSlot1) and commit(CancelParent) update both registries in one action.
required_changes.acceptance_test: Reachability: Fill1, Fill2 reaches paid 10 under both profiles. Invariant registriesCoupled holds in verify. Mutant that drops applyConsumeAuthority in commit(FillSlot1) violates registriesCoupled and enables installment-replay; mutant that edits remainingAllowance to 6 is rejected by consumption.validResidual (residual-expansion).

accepted_design_commitments: Frozen Python Core 0.0.0-e00.2 is unchanged; the common model supplies effect arithmetic and authorization predicates only, and never a shared execution interpreter for A-D; propose/observe/commitSuccessor remain per candidate.

Both signing profiles are preserved with distinct orders: SignAfterResolve is resolve, pre-sign check of the complete plan, sign, execution verification, commit; SignBeforeResolve is pre-sign check of the bounded intent and enforcement identity, sign, resolve, execution verification, commit. No before-resolve plan is ever labeled pre-sign verified.

Per-principal conjunction over debited source owners, each principal's branch checked against the complete actual effect list including incoming consideration; Bob's choice selects a branch of Alice's policy and authorizes no debit of Alice's assets.

Authorization compares effect multiplicities as multisets via effects.policyAllows; ledger application (effects.applyTransfers, canApply) and the E00 correspondence comparison are ordered. Both are recorded in the abstraction map.
Wallet and escrow locations stay distinct; a deposit is a wallet-to-escrow Transfer with no CorePayment; the frozen Core payment list is never edited to match the transfer view.

Exact-parent consumption is reused from consumption.qnt unchanged: prepared entry equality, slot ordering, residual conservation paid + remainingAllowance = 10, cancellation only with remaining allowance, revision = usedSlots + cancelled.

Recovery is independently authorized under Alice nonce 1, never reuses or reactivates nonce 0, and both paths are mandatory: cancel-wins/recovery-before-any-fill refunds ten; fill-wins/recovery-after-first-fill refunds five with slot 2 unauthorized. Existing registry witness identifiers are preserved and the two subscenario IDs are added under them.

Financial conservation escrowBalance + Wallet(Bob,TokenA) + Wallet(Alice,TokenA) = 10 is an invariant over the ledger, separate from authority; cancellation has empty effects and leaves the ledger unchanged.
Time uses concrete values 1, 2, 100, 101; physical time is monotone; stale transaction time is adversarial input and never backward physical time; environment anchor and version never wrap.
All registries and ledgers are total over finite key sets initialized at init; every action assigns every state variable; only the explicit terminal predicate admits a stutter.

Core observation carrier is lossless: total account map with zero for absent (Core forbids stored zeros), NoInt versus IntValue(0) for choices, ordered warnings with requested and paid, ordered payments with asset equal to source asset, exact error string or NoCoreError, minimum time, reductions; validation predicates encode frozen emission rules (accepted iff error absent; rejection has empty payments, warnings, zero reductions, predecessor state; accepted transactions may have zero reductions).

Deadline pair is required as hand-authored expectations: no input at 100 commits timeout refunds in canonical account order; input at 100 after timeout reduction yields contract_closed with the complete original state, continuation, minimum time, and no payments.

Evidence dispositions (signature, state, effect, assumption, settlement) are typed external premises that fail closed on Unavailable or Invalid; no model value is described as a real signature, proof, ledger execution, or Compact correspondence.

The independent E00 checker compares Python-side mapped results with hand-authored Quint expectations; the abstraction map lives on the Python side only, so a mutated map is observable as a mismatch, and for candidate A the ledger escrow balances must equal the projected Core accounts after every commit as a second, code-independent coupling check.
Architecture selection among A-D is not made by the common package or by this proposal; candidate experiments and their negative controls remain later work.
open_questions: Installment fixture timeouts: every Core When needs a timeout continuation. If it is Close, a deadline refund of the escrow exists without cancellation. Which Alice branch authorizes that refund (a deadline branch on the parent nonce 0, or the recovery nonce 1 with an AtOrAfterDeadline trigger)? Recommendation: deadline branch on nonce 0 with trigger [TimeAtOrAfter(100), NoDecision], keeping nonce 1 strictly for post-cancellation recovery.

Version bump liveness: after ImplementationV1 to V2, all V1-bound policies are permanently stale and the two-nonce budget may not allow re-signing, stranding escrow. Should such states count as terminal? Recommendation: no; report them as deadlocks and confine the version bump to a dedicated negative-control scenario rather than the positive harness step, or permit recovery policies to bind either version explicitly.

Empirical: Apalache cost of storing complete Context snapshots (registries with policies and plans) inside verification and pre-sign records for the per-kind map. If verify becomes impractical, replace snapshots by comparing the applicable bindings only (RC-13) which are far smaller; this is a modeling-cost question, not a semantic one.

Empirical: whether SignBeforeResolve residual binding for slot 2 needs a per-slot resolved plan or whether the bounded intent plus consumption.validResidual suffices; determine by attempting the residual-expansion and installment-replay mutants under that profile.

Whether a Mallory-initiated cancellation should be modeled. A shared-state model has no actor identity; the guard can only check the parent policy's CancellationRule. Recommendation: add a NotCancellable parent negative control and state actor identity as a scope limit.
Whether the E00 checker compares reductions exactly. Recommendation: yes, since the Python count is frozen and deterministic, and record it as part of the abstraction map.
implementation_order: 1. effects.qnt: add ledgerWith and installmentInitialLedger, ownerOf, and an ordered-application test; typecheck and test.

2. observations.qnt: carriers with CoreProjection, RejectionReason, NeutralInput; validCoreObservation, validFrozenCoreError, validFrozenCoreWarning, rejectionPreserved; observations_test.qnt with hand-authored expectations from core.py for the swap deadline pair, time_before_state, deposit-only accepted with zero reductions, and the A installment fixture transactions (RC-10). Freeze by hash as the split prerequisite.

3. authorization.qnt types: branch-structured Policy, validPolicy and validSignedPolicy, per-class environment freshness, finite time domain, registries with the registration supersession rule; typecheck.

4. authorization.qnt predicates: principalAllows, allAffectedPrincipalsAllow over debited owners, applicableAuthority, computeVerification, verificationValid, canCommit, registriesCoupled; unit tests for RC-01, RC-02, RC-05, RC-06, RC-14, RC-15.

5. authorization_harness.qnt, SignAfterResolve instantiation, FillSlot1 only: init, resolve, preSignCheck, sign, changeEnvironment, executionVerify, commit, rejectStale, terminalStutter; run with recorded seed; verify with Apalache and deadlock detection on.

9. Mutation pass: installment-replay, residual-expansion, post-sign-plan-substitution, omitted-state-verification, stale-recovery-plan, NotCancellable parent, drop applyConsumeAuthority, label-only outcome; record path and violated predicate for each, classify redundant defenses explicitly.
10. Pin Quint and Apalache versions and hashes, record seeds, bounds, invariant names, init and step operators, and coverage type (finite-state versus bounded-depth) in evidence/s02-model-comparison.
scope_limits: No tools were run. Quint syntax and Apalache behavior statements are derived from the supplied foundation modules and general knowledge, not from a typecheck or verify run; RC-12 acceptance tests are the discharge.

This proposal assesses only the supplied files at commits 76228d99960a78aba052aa481565d06b7a1762db and 6a60a645c03acad83b7cbc6b85d43996cd40ca65; the referenced intent.py, the Compact specialization, the S01 judgment, and the OpenSpec validator were not supplied and are not assessed.
No candidate A-D execution logic, correspondence result, proof, cryptographic claim, ledger or Compact correspondence, production cost, or architecture selection is claimed or implied.

Counterexamples are stated against the sketch's described semantics; where the sketch leaves a function unspecified, the counterexample assumes the most literal reading and RC entries state the reading used.
Actor identity is not modeled in a shared-state Quint model; who initiates an action is inferred from the policy consulted, which limits what griefing scenarios can be distinguished.
Foreman development is out of scope, and prior requests for human approval in the source documents are treated as superseded by the delegation.
Model self-identification is not evidence of provider identity, and this document is advice for design signoff, not a gate verdict.
